title: Automaker-built humanoid programs add a second high-volume entrant by Q2 2027
body: The humanoid-robot field is reorganizing around vertically-integrated, high-volume automakers that already own the motor, battery-cell, sensor, and silicon supply chains plus a consumer sales channel, rather than around standalone robotics specialists. BYD's confirmation that it is developing humanoids on shared automotive foundations - motors, batteries, electronics, precision manufacturing, and chips - with an open platform and possible dealer-network distribution gives this automaker-integrated cohort a public template and a cost-down logic borrowed directly from how BYD undercut rivals in cars. That template is reproducible by any automaker with the same in-house supply base, so the prediction is that at least one additional high-volume automaker (beyond BYD and Tesla) formally confirms or ships a humanoid program explicitly leveraging its own automotive motor, cell, or chip supply chain by the end of Q2 2027. Confirmation should arrive as an on-record executive disclosure, a working prototype, or a stated production or cost-down target tied to existing vehicle manufacturing - the markers that separate a real integrated program from a press-release partnership with an outside robotics vendor. The signal to watch is whether the entrant frames the robot as an extension of its existing powertrain and electronics stack, which is what distinguishes the integrated cohort from a badge-engineered reseller.

reasoning.because: BYD confirmed a humanoid program built on its in-house auto motor, cell, and chip supply base
reasoning.given: Any high-volume automaker owning the same motor/cell/silicon stack can copy the cost-down playbook
reasoning.so_that: At least one more high-volume automaker confirms or ships a humanoid program leveraging its own auto supply chain
reasoning.landing: By end of Q2 2027; one new automaker via disclosure, prototype, or target
reasoning.plain_language: Carmakers that already make their own motors, batteries, and chips can build robots cheaply, so another big carmaker will join the race soon.

summary: BYD's confirmed humanoid program, built on its in-house auto motor, cell, and chip supply, hands high-volume automakers a reproducible cost-down template for embodied AI. Expect one more automaker beyond BYD and Tesla to confirm or ship an integrated humanoid program by end of Q2 2027.
